q: Fouché's theorem on algorithmic randomness of chaotic orbits states that for the doubling map and Lebesgue measure:
opts: x has a ML-random binary expansion iff the symbolic orbit is ML-random as a sequence
ML-random x have eventually periodic orbits
exp: Fouché: x is ML-random iff its orbit sequence (binary expansion) is ML-random. ML-random points form a measure-1 set; computable initial conditions give periodic/eventually periodic orbits — never random. Randomness comes from the initial condition, not the map.
